title: P5 design RAG — event store, collision, pagination and observability

sections.title: P5 design RAG — event store, collision, pagination and observability
sections.text:
**Verified:** 2026-09-19  
**Boundary:** External sources constrain append/idempotency, SQL identity/RETURNING and metric-cardinality **properties**.
Agentools class names, ALC seq numbering (first event `seq=1`, empty stream `expected_prev_seq=0`), tenant isolation, error codes, audit kinds and phase ownership are repository design decisions (`RAG:—`), not claims sourced from Kurrent/EventStoreDB, PostgreSQL or OpenTelemetry.

Perplexity was queried twice through the configured `plugin-core-perplexity` MCP: one web+academic synthesis of EventStoreDB/Kurrent atomic batch append, expected revision and EventId idempotency versus PostgreSQL `INSERT`/`RETURNING`, and one web synthesis of Prometheus/OpenTelemetry metric cardinality. Every load-bearing claim below was then rechecked against the linked primary source. Native WebFetch succeeded for Kurrent TCP appending, PostgreSQL `INSERT`, Prometheus instrumentation, and the OpenTelemetry Metrics SDK. The 2026 OTel cardinality blog timed out; the SDK spec is the primary for overflow/limit numbers.

| Evidence | Verified claim | P5 consequence |
|:--|:--|:--|
| RAG:✅ [Kurrent/EventStoreDB TCP appending](https://docs.kurrent.io/clients/tcp/dotnet/21.2/appending), accessed 2026-09-19 | One operation appends one or more events **atomically**. Optimistic concurrency uses `expectedVersion` (numeric, `NoStream`/`EmptyStream`/`StreamExists`, or `Any` to disable). Identical appends are idempotent **if** the concurrency check is not disabled. Idempotence is based on `EventId` **and stream**; EventIds may be reused across streams. With a numeric expected version, `expected < current` compares EventIds from that point: all already committed → success without duplicates; none committed → `WrongExpectedVersion`; **some** committed → bad request / `WrongExpectedVersion`. `ExpectedVersion.Any` does **not** guarantee idempotence. Batch length must not exceed 4095. | Keep atomic batch + expected stream version. Do **not** expose `Any`. Treat partial overlap as a typed conflict, not a silent append. Agentools strengthens EventId-only match with a content hash (F05). 4095 is not the Agentools batch cap. |
| RAG:✅ [Kurrent Python appending / idempotent append](https://docs.kurrent.io/clients/python/v1.2/appending-events.md), accessed 2026-09-19 | Event IDs activate idempotent append; KurrentDB **does not enforce** unique event IDs. Retry of a successful append with OCC on returns without failing. Same ID on a different stream, or on the same stream with a later correct expected version, can record more than one event with that ID. | Unique `(tenant_id, event_id)` is an Agentools invariant, not a Kurrent port. Retry must keep the same IDs **and** the original expected version. |
| RAG:✅ [PostgreSQL `INSERT`](https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/sql-insert.html), accessed 2026-09-19 | `RETURNING` returns only rows **actually inserted or updated**. `ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING` does not return the conflicting row. `GENERATED ALWAYS AS IDENTITY` rejects an explicit value unless `OVERRIDING SYSTEM VALUE`. | Classify replay vs collision **before** INSERT, under a stream lock. Do not use `DO NOTHING RETURNING` as the collision detector. `global_position` is IDENTITY; callers never supply it. |
| RAG:✅ [PostgreSQL identity columns](https://www.postgresql.org/docs/18/ddl-identity-columns.html) and [RETURNING](https://www.postgresql.org/docs/18/dml-returning.html), accessed 2026-09-19 | Identity values are sequence-generated when omitted/`DEFAULT`. `RETURNING` is the supported way to read assigned defaults in the same statement. | AppendResult reads `stream_seq` and `global_position` from `RETURNING`, not a follow-up SELECT. Content hash must not include IDENTITY columns. |
| RAG:✅ [RFC 8785 JCS](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc8785.html), already verified for PLAN1 foundations, still current 2026-09-19 | Canonical JSON is deterministic property order/serialization under I-JSON constraints. | Collision/idempotency digest is `sha-256:` + SHA-256 of JCS bytes of the uncommitted envelope **excluding** storage-assigned fields. P6 still owns the cross-language JCS oracle. |
| RAG:✅ [Prometheus instrumentation](https://prometheus.io/docs/practices/instrumentation/), accessed 2026-09-19 | Each labelset is a time series. Guideline: keep cardinality of most metrics below 10; metrics that exceed that should be a handful system-wide. Cardinality over 100 (or unbounded growth) should leave monitoring. | Metric labels are a closed low-cardinality set. `tenant_id`, `action_id`, `event_id`, `trace_id` are forbidden metric labels. |
| RAG:✅ [OpenTelemetry Metrics SDK](https://opentelemetry.io/docs/specs/otel/metrics/sdk/), accessed 2026-09-19 | Default `aggregation_cardinality_limit` SHOULD be 2000. Overflow aggregates leftover measurements under `otel.metric.overflow=true`. Overflow is a memory guardrail: totals can remain, breakdowns become incomplete. | Cardinality policy is fail-closed at the Agentools adapter (reject/drop the label), not “rely on SDK overflow”. No OpenTelemetry SDK runtime dependency. |

sections.title: Facts intentionally not promoted
sections.text:
- Kurrent `ExpectedVersion.Any`, `-2`, 0-based revisions, 4095 batch cap, 16 MiB event size, and TCP transactions are product choices of that store, not Agentools defaults. Empty stream remains `expected_prev_seq=0` / first `seq=1` (ALC-6/20).
- EventStoreDB matching EventIds without comparing payloads is **weaker** than F05. Silent ID-only no-op is the current InMemory/SQLite defect.
- Prometheus “below 10” is a guideline, not a hard platform limit. P5 still forbids unbounded identifiers as labels.
- OTel semantic-convention `gen_ai.*` names live in an optional export adapter (AOB-25/26/27), not in the journal schema. P6 may pin mapping version; P5 only forbids leaking audit-forbidden fields (AOB-14/16/28).
- Audit SQL `agentools_action_events` and `EventStore` PHP sketches are F14, not schema.
